correctness.rationale: The adjacency identity A²=(k−μ)I+(λ−μ)A+μJ yields the two nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues and, by the trace, their multiplicities. On the complement of the constants both eigenspaces must occur, since otherwise all off-diagonal Laplacian entries would coincide. Interpolation on 0,a,b gives the stated common diagonal and the two off-diagonal formulas. I independently expanded the numerators of r′ and q′, q=(1−r)/t: −24(t⁴−30t²+600) and −2(t⁴+120t²+1200t+3600), respectively, over D². Each is strictly negative; for z>0, the nonedge entry is a positive multiple of q(az)−q(bz), and the edge correction has the sign of r(az)−r(bz). The diagonal decreases strictly from 1 to (2−v)/v<0; clearing the positive denominators gives one positive root and a degree-six polynomial with leading coefficient (ab)³(2−v)≠0. At h=0 the map is the identity. The rational root comparisons and illustrative cases agree with the proof.
residual_risks: Finite floating-point examples are diagnostics, not the universal proof; no inference on intermediate stages, nonuniform conductances, or floating-point implementation.
